coefplot

Coefficient plot

Stata 

coefplot

R modelsummary 

modelsummary::modelplot(fit)

Stata reference · R reference

graph

Bar chart of counts

Stata 

graph bar (count), over(x)

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_bar()

Stata reference · R reference

Bar chart of group means

Stata 

graph bar (mean) y, over(group)

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar")

Stata reference · R reference

Box plot

Stata 

graph box y, over(group)

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(group, y)) + geom_boxplot()

Differs from Stata ggplot2 boxplot hinges use R quantile rules; Stata uses Stata percentiles, which may differ in small samples and with ties.

Stata reference · R reference

Save the last graph

Stata 

graph export figure.png

R ggplot2 

ggsave("figure.png")

Stata reference · R reference

Pie chart

Stata 

graph pie, over(group)

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(x = "", fill = group)) + geom_bar() + coord_polar(theta = "y")

Stata reference · R reference

Label summary bars with their values

Stata 

graph bar (mean) y, over(group) blabel(bar)

R ggplot2 

{ plot_data <- aggregate(y ~ group, data, mean); ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(group, y)) + ggplot2::geom_col() + ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = round(y, 1)), vjust = -0.3) }

Differs from Stata Reproduces the displayed count, percent or summary layer, rather than Stata graph display defaults. Match category order and missingness; ggplot themes, axis scales and bar annotations follow R conventions.

Stata reference · R reference

Plot group percentages

Stata 

graph bar (percent), over(group)

R ggplot2 

{ counts <- as.data.frame(table(data$group)); ggplot2::ggplot(counts, ggplot2::aes(Var1, Freq / sum(Freq) * 100)) + ggplot2::geom_col() }

Differs from Stata Reproduces the displayed count, percent or summary layer, rather than Stata graph display defaults. Match category order and missingness; ggplot themes, axis scales and bar annotations follow R conventions.

histogram

Histogram

Stata 

histogram x

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_histogram()

Differs from Stata geom_histogram() defaults to counts and 30 bins; Stata histogram defaults to density with a different bin rule. Specify breaks/binwidth and the y statistic.

Stata reference · R reference

6 more examples and alternatives

Compare histograms across groups

Stata 

histogram y, by(group)

R ggplot2 

ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(y)) + ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 10) + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~group)

Differs from Stata Set boundaries and interval closure explicitly when matching Stata bin counts.

Stata reference · R reference

kdensity

Density plot

Stata 

kdensity x, kernel(gaussian) bwidth(1)

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(x)) + geom_density(kernel = "gaussian", bw = 1)

Differs from Stata Both specify a Gaussian kernel and bandwidth 1. Default kdensity uses Epanechnikov, unlike default geom_density. Density grids/rendering may differ.

Stata reference · R reference

4 more examples and alternatives

Estimate a density for a subgroup

Stata 

kdensity y if group == "A", kernel(gaussian) bwidth(1)

R ggplot2 

ggplot2::ggplot(subset(data, group == "A"), ggplot2::aes(y)) + ggplot2::geom_density(kernel = "gaussian", bw = 1)

Differs from Stata Both specify Gaussian kernel and bandwidth 1; evaluation grids and rendering may differ.

line

Line plot

Stata 

line y x

R ggplot2 

ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_line()

Differs from Stata geom_line() sorts by x within groups; Stata line/connected uses observation order without the sort option.

Stata reference · R reference

3 more examples and alternatives

Line plot sorted by the horizontal variable

Stata 

line y x, sort

R ggplot2 

ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) + ggplot2::geom_line()

Differs from Stata Maps the stated axes and layer; line sorts by x in ggplot while Stata uses sort here. Plot themes, axis expansion, missing-point warnings and facet scales follow R defaults.

Differs from Stata Maps the stated axes and layer; line sorts by x in ggplot while Stata uses sort here. Plot themes, axis expansion, missing-point warnings and facet scales follow R defaults.

lowess

Smoothed scatter plot

Stata 

lowess y x

R stats 

{ smooth <- stats::lowess(data$x, data$y, f = 0.8, iter = 0, delta = 0); graphics::plot(data$x, data$y); graphics::lines(smooth) }

Differs from Stata Nonrobust local-linear tricube LOWESS with span 0.8; disables R robustness iterations and interpolation skipping. Neighborhood and tie rules may still differ.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Draw a local regression smooth

Stata 

lowess y x, bwidth(0.5)

R stats 

{ smooth <- stats::lowess(data$x, data$y, f = 0.5, iter = 0, delta = 0); graphics::plot(data$x, data$y); graphics::lines(smooth) }

Differs from Stata Local-linear tricube smoothing with span 0.5; iter=0 disables robust reweighting and delta=0 disables interpolation skipping. Neighborhood and tie rules may differ.

Stata reference · R reference

pchi

Compare empirical and chi-squared probabilities

Stata 

pchi y, df(2)

R graphics 

{ values <- sort(data$y[!is.na(data$y)]); positions <- seq_along(values) / (length(values) + 1); graphics::plot(positions, stats::pchisq(values, df = 2), xlab = "Empirical", ylab = "Chi-squared CDF"); graphics::abline(0, 1) }

Differs from Stata Uses Weibull positions i/(N+1) with the specified chi-squared CDF.

Stata reference · R reference

pnorm

Assess a standardized normal P-P relationship

Stata 

pnorm y

R graphics 

{ values <- sort(data$y[!is.na(data$y)]); positions <- seq_along(values) / (length(values) + 1); graphics::plot(positions, stats::pnorm((values - mean(values)) / stats::sd(values)), xlab = "Empirical", ylab = "Normal"); graphics::abline(0, 1) }

Differs from Stata Uses Weibull positions i/(N+1) and sample mean/SD, as Stata pnorm.

Stata reference · R reference

qchi

Compare sample quantiles with chi-squared quantiles

Stata 

qchi y, df(2)

R graphics 

{ values <- sort(data$y[!is.na(data$y)]); positions <- seq_along(values) / (length(values) + 1); graphics::plot(stats::qchisq(positions, df = 2), values, xlab = "Chi-squared quantile", ylab = "y"); graphics::abline(0, 1) }

Differs from Stata Uses Weibull positions i/(N+1) with the specified chi-squared distribution.

Stata reference · R reference

qnorm

Normal quantile plot

Stata 

qnorm x

R graphics 

{ values <- sort(data$x[!is.na(data$x)]); p <- seq_along(values) / (length(values) + 1); graphics::plot(mean(values) + sd(values) * qnorm(p), values, xlab = "Inverse normal", ylab = "x"); graphics::abline(0, 1) }

Differs from Stata Uses Stata Weibull positions i/(N+1) and sample mean/SD scaling, rather than default ggplot standard-normal quantiles.

Stata reference · R reference

qqplot

Compare two empirical distributions with a Q-Q plot

Stata 

qqplot y x

R stats 

stats::qqplot(data$x, data$y)

Differs from Stata A diagnostic plotting workflow; plotting-position and standardization defaults can differ from Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

quantile

Plot ordered data against cumulative fractions

Stata 

quantile y

R graphics 

{ values <- sort(data$y[!is.na(data$y)]); positions <- (seq_along(values) - 0.5) / length(values); graphics::plot(positions, values, xlab = "Fraction", ylab = "y") }

Differs from Stata Uses Hazen positions (i-0.5)/N at every sample size, as Stata quantile.
